subject: Re: DPA redline — regional residency, analytics subprocessor variance

Subject: Initial redline + residency ask

Hi Grace / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team attached a marked-up DPA (attached) with two items blocking execution:

1) Residency: We need confirmation that telemetry used for analytics can be restricted to US regions only. Our security policy requires provider telemetry for inference to remain in-country (US) unless explicit customer opt-in.

2) Subprocessor variance: We noted an allowed subprocessor clause that permits regional analytics vendors. We need clarity and either an explicit allowlist or a variance approval process (particularly for APAC vendors).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a US-only residency commitment for telemetry and provide an auditable subprocessor variance path? If not, what mitigations (contract language) do you propose?

I attached the redline PDF. We are aiming to close by 04/25 to meet internal go-live.

Thanks,
Jamie

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear summary and the timeline. Looping in Legal (Olga) and Product (Karthik) for the two asks.

A couple quick clarifying questions so we route correctly:
- When you say "telemetry used for analytics", do you mean aggregate inference telemetry (latency/cost tokens), or will this include any inference payloads/outputs?
- For the subprocessor variance, are you seeking pre-approval of specific vendors we listed, or a contractual mechanism to request/approve new ones?

High level: we try to avoid committing to region-specific persistent storage for all telemetry by default because a portion of our operational telemetry flows through multi-region pipelines (metrics, rollups). That said, we can propose a scoped carveout that treats customer-facing inference payloads differently (e.g., runtime KV cache snapshots and outputs) and keep aggregate/system telemetry in our standard observability pipelines.

Olga / Karthik — flagged as 'needs review'. Please see Jamie's redline and the specific asks re: residency + subproc governance. Can we get recommendations and whether Product is comfortable with a scoped carveout?

Date: 2028-04-19T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — residency & subprocessor variance (legal comments)

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the redline and the two asks. High-level legal position: we cannot wholesale guarantee that every telemetry stream will be physically stored exclusively in the US for all customers under our current hosted runtime architecture. However, we can offer a combination of contractual and operational mitigations:

1) Contractual carveout (proposed language): we will treat "customer-designated inference payloads" as protected telemetry and limit their persistence to US regions for Acme's tenant. Non-customer-designated operational telemetry (system metrics, anonymized routing logs) will remain in our standard telemetry pipelines. This is a targeted residency commitment, not a global product change.

2) Subprocessor variance process: we can add a clause that requires Redwood to notify Acme of any new analytics subprocessor 30 days prior to onboarding and to provide a variance request packet (vendor name, region, SOC reports, data flows). The contract will give Acme the right to object within 14 days; if Acme objects, Redwood will either (a) not route Acme's telemetry through that vendor for a specified period, or (b) provide a compensating control.

Technical questions for Product (Karthik) before we finalize wording:
- Can Product identify the exact telemetry types that can be scoped to US-only for a single tenant today (e.g., KV snapshots, output logs, request/response payloads)?
- What are the runtime implications if we isolate those streams per-tenant (cost, latency, operational overhead)?

I will draft proposed redline language once Product confirms the scoping.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Counsel, Security & Privacy — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redline — residency & subprocessor variance (product impact)

Thanks — quick product assessment:

Short answer: we can scoped-effectively support the carveout Olga proposes for a single tenant, but there are tradeoffs. Details: 

- What we can isolate today with reasonable effort: request/response payloads (if customer opts out of cross-region mirroring), KV cache snapshots (we can pin their persistence to a US-only storage tier), and exported inference output logs. These are the primary telemetry categories Acme seems to be concerned about.

- What we cannot easily isolate without product/planning work: aggregated system metrics and multi-region routing metadata. Those are baked into our global observability pipeline and would require a cross-team engineering project to segregate per-tenant.

Operational impacts:
- Cost: US-only persistence for the identified artifacts would increase per-GB storage cost (~10–15%) and add egress overhead when customers access aggregated dashboards (if dashboards are served from multi-region services).
- Latency: minimal for inference runtime; slight added latency when reconstructing cross-region analytics views in the console.
- Implementation timeline: we can ship a tenant-scoped residency carveout as a configuration path in our private/hosted stack in ~6–8 weeks with a focused engineering task (workaround already exists in our Dedicated product).

Suggested contract language options for Olga: 
A) Targeted residency promise (preferred): "Redwood will persist Customer-Designated Inference Artifacts in US regions only for the duration of the Agreement for Acme Health, subject to the operational controls listed in Schedule X."

B) Process + fallback (if Acme needs pre-approval for subprocessors): "Redwood will provide 30 days' notice of any new analytics subprocessor and supply documentation sufficient for Security review. If Customer objects, Redwood will: (i) not route Customer-Designated Inference Artifacts to the objected subprocessor; or (ii) provide a documented compensating control."

We can accept either and provide an SOW addendum for the minor engineering work (recommended if Acme needs stricter assurances).

Happy to jump on a quick call with Jamie to walk through the technical tradeoffs.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product — Redwood Inference

Jamie / Jordan —

Thanks for your patience. Based on legal + product feedback above, we've prepared a revised DPA with the scoped residency carveout and a subprocessor variance process. Summary of changes: 

• Residency carveout: "Customer-Designated Inference Artifacts" (defined in Schedule 1) will be persisted only in US regions for Acme's tenant. Non-designated operational telemetry remains in Redwood's standard telemetry systems.

• Subprocessor variance: Redwood will notify Acme 30 days prior to onboarding any new analytics subprocessor and will provide a vendor packet. Acme may object within 14 days; on objection Redwood will not route Customer-Designated Inference Artifacts to that vendor.
